title: Phased retirement for graph.generate & bulk-embed: SDK auto-adaptor playbook
creator: Maya Patel
description: Context: Two legacy contracts are still widely used in client integrations: graph.generate (multiplexed request-response over legacy stream routing) and bulk-embed (batch embeddings long-polling). These contracts differ from the unified /v1/infer schema and cause maintenance overhead in routing, monitoring, and our SLA guarantees. Goal: retire both legacy contracts with minimal customer friction by providing: (1) a phased timeline, (2) SDK auto-adaptors for major languages, (3) server-side backward-compat fallback for a defined grace period, (4) telemetry gates, and (5) clear communication and rollback criteria. This ticket is the product playbook and acceptance criteria; engineering tickets will be created from the migration_steps list below. Scope clarifications: - We will NOT perform any server-side behavior changes to payload semantics during the grace period (only compatibility translations) to avoid breaking clients. - We will require opt-in telemetry for clients using deprecated endpoints to build migration cohorts. - Dedicated customers with SLA contracts can request extended grace periods via account teams (handled outside this ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Public deprecation announcement published with exact timeline and migration guides
Language SDKs (JavaScript, Python, Go) include opt-in auto-adaptor version that rewrites legacy calls to unified API and is available in major package managers
Server-side compatibility layer will accept legacy payloads and map them to the unified model for a fixed 12-week grace period after GA of SDK adaptors
Telemetry surfaces: deprecated_endpoint=true attribute emitted in request logs and routed to Console Usage and Migration dashboards
Migration runbook and rollback criteria documented and validated with one customer pilot
No increase in critical errors (5xx) attributable to migration beyond 0.5% of baseline during pilot and staged rollout
Client-facing docs include code samples, rate-limiting differences, and model alias mapping table
Legal/Compliance sign-off for data retention changes and audit logs is completed
Product/Support playbook for billing adjustments and grace exceptions is published
All related engineering tickets have owners and clear test plans attached
migration_steps: Inventory active callers from traffic bucket and customer telemetry; prioritize top 40 customers by request volume
Implement SDK auto-adaptors: JS (npm), Py (pip), Go (gopkg) with configurable opt-in flag 'redwood_compat=1'
Build server-side compatibility proxy to accept legacy contracts and emit mapped unified requests internally
Add telemetry flags and vanity metrics to Console: deprecated_endpoint, migration_stage, adaptor_version
Create pilot cohort with 3 customers (1 startup, 1 mid-market, 1 enterprise) for integration testing
Iterate based on pilot feedback and fix edge cases around streaming truncation and embedding length limits
Start staged rollout: beta (SDK users only) -> staged opt-in (webhooks/email customers) -> announced enforcement
Enforce retirement by soft-failure (HTTP 426/410 header + guidance) for 4 weeks, then hard reject after extended notice
Post-retirement: remove compatibility proxy and mark metrics as deprecated in Console after 12 weeks
rollout_timeline: Week 0: Publish deprecation notice + migration guide. Weeks 1-4: SDK auto-adaptor beta and pilot. Weeks 5-8: Staged opt-in rollout with telemetry gates. Weeks 9-12: Soft-fail enforcement window with account outreach. Week 16: Hard cutoff for legacy endpoints for all self-serve accounts; Dedicated customers handled case-by-case. Post-cutoff +12 weeks: remove compatibility proxy and cleanup internal routing configs.
communication_plan: 1) Public blog + Console banner with timeline and link to migration guide. 2) Targeted emails to top 40 customers and account team playbook. 3) Support KB articles and migration checklist. 4) SDK release notes include migration notes and automatic adaptors. 5) Community Slack/Discord + Office hours weekly during staged rollout.
client_sdk_changes: JS SDK: new CompatShim class and 'autoCompat' boolean flag. Default false. If true, legacy calls are rewritten client-side.
Python SDK: redwood.compat.enable_auto_adaptor() opt-in helper and detailed logger for translated payloads
Go SDK: compatibility module with functional shim and backoff behaviors aligned with unified API
All SDKs: telemetry opt-in header 'X-Redwood-Compat: 1' added when adaptors active
telemetry_requirements: Emit 'deprecated_endpoint' boolean on every proxied request
Track adaptor_version and client_sdk_version in request logs
Build migration dashboard with daily active deprecated-callers, success rate, mean latency delta
Gate progression to wider rollout on 99th percentile latency delta < 50ms and error rate delta < 0.5%
Alert on anomalous spikes in 4xx/5xx from adaptor users (pager duty to infra on threshold)
review_feedback: Design: Ensure examples cover streaming truncation edge cases (Claire Wong)
Eng Infra: Recommend gradual rollout with circuit breaker on proxy to protect runtime (Liam O'Connor)
Security: Confirm telemetry headers do not leak PII and add KMS usage note (Anika Rao)
Support: Provide canned responses and escalations for enterprise accounts (Jordan Blake)
notes: Trade-offs discussed: client-side adaptors minimize server cost but rely on clients updating SDKs; server proxy provides broad coverage but increases runtime complexity.
Decision: Combine both approaches — release SDK adaptors first and run proxy only for customers who opt-in or fail to migrate by soft-fail window.
Risk: Long-lived clients behind NATs may not receive banners; account outreach required for top volume customers.
Pilot outcome criteria documented in pilot-retrospective doc linked above
